due_why: Its owner, 2DZF5Z, given it by the orchestrator on 22 Nov after its date of 21 Nov passed with it failing 6 of the 39 net runs from 20 Nov 19:27 to 22 Nov 05:23 UTC. In all six, calendars_from_now pressed Return on Date's Calendars while that row still read Calendars with an ellipsis, asking, just after timekeeping.socket started again, and that row's Return only closed, so the launcher closed under Joel's way to the calendars. Ask 203 (#6078) makes Return on it step in, to a place the calendars fill as they come, which the-launcher-names-the-parts-it-builds proves on every run in Qt's engine; with a drop-in giving timekeeping.service ExecStartPre=sleep 15, run by run-subtests, the old launcher fails at that Return and the new one passes. It comes off once twenty net runs in a row after the fix exit 0, counted by exit code, since a failure only here is recorded as passed: at 6 in 39, twenty pass by luck about one time in thirty. A launcher closed at that Return means the fix is wrong. A wait for the four calendars that runs out, its 60 s covering the reader's start, means the fix is wrong if the journal says 'calendars held' at any point after the socket started again while the step still holds no rows, and a slow or hung reader if it doesn't; back at Date means the reader refused. Only a closed launcher and an answer that never filled the step count against the fix; any other failure restarts the count. If twenty in a row haven't passed by the end of 24 Nov UTC, its owner moves the due and sends the new one before this one passes. Firmware, listed beside it, came off on 22 Nov: all seven net runs after #5869 passed it, six exiting 0 and one failing only the time here. While it stands, nothing catches a change that breaks what the subtest checks: Date's calendars with the reader gone and back, the clock's figures, chrony's servers and their drawers, Time with chronyd stopped, and Time keeping one Clock when its reader answers late

Its owner, the call shaper's, read on 23 Nov where the calls' datagrams went in the net's runs that lost past the bar, and the fix that answers what was the builder's (#6406, declaring the rig's line at its slowest busy hour) landed on 24 Nov as b92e4d47. At its head test_a_call_loses_little passed 9 of 10 fresh runs on the builder that failed it, its one failure the router's queue dropping 530 of the download to the IFB's 5 while the room held, a cause not yet named; test_a_call_goes_ahead_of_its_own_uploads failed 3 of 9 there, its classes at 6035 under a 6000 trial, a cut to 4770 under it, and 56 video drops. In 10 runs at 82420a60 it failed 2, cuts to 4645 and 5368, and test_a_call_loses_little 1, a fill that timed out. Both cuts came in seconds whose trace reads no ceiling, and the trial's ceiling held only 82 and 61 s after them, so it took late, for a reason not yet named, and the controller cut on its own. #6456 has the subtest wait until the shaper's newest second holds the trial's ceiling, failing with the trace if it never does, and prints each second's ask, ceiling, room and reason, so the next such failure says whether the trial took and why the controller cut; the wait now also reads the upload's classes and the trial file's time, and says how long the ceiling took on a pass. In 5 runs at 9b791623, whose wait read only the trace's ceiling, not yet the classes, test_a_call_goes_ahead_of_its_own_uploads passed all 5, and test_a_call_loses_little failed 1, the IFB dropping 4 of the download to the router's queue's 813. With the shaper stopped on 20 Nov (00ddeee71091), the client's own receive buffers overflowed, 376 datagrams, iperf3 starved on the builder: the calls' sockets now have room for seconds of datagrams, and the bar counts only what was lost before the client's socket. Shaped in that run, the shaper's IFB dropped them, media's 12 all in its video tin and the page call's beside the app's downloads in best effort; and on 20 Nov (f0197badd1be) the router's down queue dropped 441 of the media call while nothing limited the download. Those two, both in shaped subtests, are the shaper's to prevent, so they still count against the bar, and a run that loses so again shows the shaper's own drops by tin, and what went missing between the router's count and the client's input hook, which the router's queue, the wire, the shaper's IFB or the client's own receive path took, the IFB's share named by its drops. The router's are the download hold's to prevent (jitsusama/shaper-holds-the-download-for-a-call): while a call is on and the download carries nine tenths of its declared 75 Mbit/s, under the router's 90, or the controller cuts it, the shaper holds it there, so it queues in the IFB's CAKE, where the call goes first, and that fix moved the due from 2026-11-27. A handshake reply lost coming down failed a call on 22 Nov (519b71b08ac0) with a stale errno, and is now made again as any lost handshake is, but only while the shaper's IFB dropped nothing meanwhile in the video and voice tins a call comes down in, so one lost while the shaper's own call tins dropped still fails. Every machine on a call's path now counts its datagrams each way, printed on a pass too, and a count under what iperf3 read fails, so a counter that misses the call can't read as nothing lost. test_a_call_loses_little bars a hundredth of a call lost coming down before the client's socket, and test_a_call_goes_ahead_of_its_own_uploads a hundredth of it dropped by the shaper's video tin going up. Its due, which its owner takes as 1 Dec at 18:00 EST though the hourly loop counts it late only from 2 Dec, is three days after the fix for what those traces name lands, by 28 Nov 18:00 EST; the twenty net runs in a row it needs after that fix take about two days and a quarter at the net's pace of about nine a day, which leaves about seven runs' room; at 3 failing runs in 10, as at 82420a60, twenty pass in a row by luck under once in a thousand, so it can't come off without that fix. If that fix isn't in by 28 Nov 18:00 EST, or a red run past the seventh after it starts the count again, its owner sends a new due before this one passes. It comes off once twenty net runs in a row after that fix exit 0, counted by exit code, since a failure only here is recorded as passed. Before: the net excused 7 failures from 14 to 18 Nov, and about 5 in 20 runs failed after its failure trace was added, each a call losing 69 to 3,106 datagrams down, once with the shaper stopped, or the shaper not holding within 60 s, which #5897's asking a dark network again soon answered: none of the 15 net runs since it failed so. test_a_call_goes_ahead_of_its_own_uploads joined it on 20 Nov for sharing that holding wait and the call's bars, not for a failure of its own, though it has failed on its own since, as above, and while it is listed a failure in it alone is said and blocks nothing, before a merge or after, so until it comes off nothing catches a change that stops telling Joel's CAKE its rate: the unit tests cover only the rate chosen and the command's form

Its owner, the shaper's, found the cause on 23 Nov, and its fix, the client's second core, landed that day in #6254 (b0e93c56); the net runs counted since it decide by 2026-11-27 18:00 EST, a day before its due, whether it comes off. The test's client ran on one core: at b18b11bc945b its CAKE sent under the shaper's limit with data waiting and its kernel said htb had too many events, so the shaper, reading the client's own sending as the line's, cut again a second after its first cut, to 5391, and learned a plateau of 5280 to hold under, a median of 5016. The shaper climbs only while the client carries three quarters of its limit, so a client that falls behind drifts toward such a plateau instead, which is how the halved rate stayed low after the link came back. Neither is the shaper's on a real line: the owner's record of 22 Nov holds 1,312 cuts, and none of the 11 that came within 3 s of the one before stacked downward. The fix gives the client a second core, and a passing run prints its median, each reading's rate beside what the link's queues sent and held waiting, naming a client that fell behind, and the climb, from what rate and how long. It comes off once twenty net runs in a row after the fix exit 0 and their printed medians, readings and climbs show no client falling behind: at the 8 in 61 rate of 16 to 19 Nov ten pass by luck one time in four, but at the one failure in 30 seen since, twenty pass by luck about half the time, so the count alone can't show a fix. A red run past the seventh run after the fix, which starts the count again, moves the due. 8 of 61 net runs from 16 to 19 Nov exited 1, and each of the six whose logs remain held the upload under 6000, three failing here at medians of 5754 to 5887 and three timing out in a fixture, once never finding the connection in 90 s, at 4158, and twice never climbing back past 6000 from the halved rate in 120 s, once reaching 4880, as one failing here did too, still at 3923. While it stands, a run whose failed subtests are all listed, any of this one and the entry below's two, is excused whole, the net naming a subtest whose fixture timed out as failed, and so is one that loses its machine after them, its later lines dropped, but one cut off at its time limit names no subtest and is excused by nothing; a timeout in loaded names all six and isn't excused. Every other check in this subtest goes unguarded, among them its 8800 ceiling, answered pings, 80 ms ping bound, pings ending within 60 s and the shaper's status file being there
reason: failed on main at 89dc01f5ad2a twice, 3c36b575e846, 38063460e6a0, e3932cb77356 twice and 7030d16c46ae twice, passing between; #5615, the Mycelium lock where the net last met it, didn't cause it

due_why: Its owner, the shaper's, found its cause with the entry above's on 23 Nov, and the same fix, the client's second core, landed that day in #6254 (b0e93c56): the returned fixture these two share timed out at b18b11bc945b, never climbing back past 6000 in 120 s, in the run in which test_finds_the_connection held a median of 5016 under its floor, since a client that falls behind its limit drifts toward the plateau it learned rather than climbing. While it stands, a run whose failed subtests are any of these two and test_finds_the_connection is excused whole, so nothing catches the shaper not climbing back after the link returns, eth2 not taking eth1's rate, the recorder not counting eth2, or the upload not held under the halved rate on a second link. Before the fix, test_second_link put the rig back only at its end, so failing before eth2's uploads started left eth1's stopped, and failing in its halved hold left eth2's uploads running on a halved connection, either way failing test_unshaped after it, unexcused. Its owner, ISXEG8, who owns the fence's strength, took it on 24 Nov from the orchestrator. The subtest it names is an X11 window of Joel's taking the focus, and past it the secret copy's phase, split on 24 Nov from test_a_fenced_command_reads_no_secret_copy_through_x11, which isn't listed and fails the net's run as any subtest does. That one asserts in every run the line saying the fence's walls held, which are tried before any window takes the focus; where the satellite's two steps held, it asserts the script ended clean, and where one didn't, it takes only that step's own failure as the ending, 'niri focused no X11 window' or, past the focus, 'Joel's own X11 client didn't read his copy', so a run stopped at either fails the listed subtest alone and any other failure fails the unlisted one too. The precondition failed 6 of the net's 62 runs from 20 to 23 Nov, at a60435126103, 40c0beb33200 twice, ad1d4fc0cfb4, b5acf904044f and 3bdb3ff3d5ab, each with the script's 'niri focused no X11 window' and never a line of the fence's: xlogo opened and niri focused no window for a minute, and the satellite's log met xlogo's window only as the test killed it, saying it couldn't get the pid of a window whose program had gone. Of the 45 net logs still kept at 09:30 on 24 Nov, the 4 failures among them say that and never 'No last focused toplevel', the 37 other runs that reached the satellite say 'No last focused toplevel' and never the pid line, and 4 cut short have no satellite lines. Reading xwayland-satellite, xcb queues the events it reads while a request waits for a reply, and the main loop then polls the socket over them, so the window's CreateNotify waited for the next event; upstream fixed that in 779151fdfc, which modules/niri/drain-buffered-events.patch backports. It comes off once twenty net runs in a row after that patch merges pass this subtest, about a day and a half at the net's 62 runs in four days. The count only shows nothing else broke: at 6 in 62, twenty pass by luck about one time in eight, and the evidence for the fix is upstream's diagnosis, which the logs above fit. Any failure of this subtest resets the count, its log kept or not; a run red only elsewhere neither counts nor resets it. Its owner reads the net's logs of this test each day while the entry stands, and each failing run's log the day it fails. On any reset its owner moves the due and says why. One whose satellite log says it couldn't get the window's pid failed the same way, so the patch didn't fix the cause, and its owner finds it. Any other failure of it, a crash of the satellite or the test's own error among them, is its owner's to fix forward that day, or to revert the patch through the gate when the patch caused it. Taking the entry off alone reverts nothing. While it stands, a run stopped at either of the satellite's steps still proves every wall of the fence's, since refusing a connection owes nothing to what the clipboard holds, but with no secret copy on it, so in those runs alone nothing that blocks a merge catches Joel's own X11 client no longer reading his copies through the satellite

due_why: Its owner, the margin cat's, takes it off once twenty net runs in a row exit 0 after the fix for its cause merges. It failed at a6901f968d03 and on a loaded lender at 847f070456cd the same way: the cat drew 8 frames of its own under the launcher, {'cat winit': 8, 'launcher': 8}, while its still neighbours drew none. The cause, found on 23 Nov: Joel's shell unit sets QT_WAYLAND_FRAME_CALLBACK_TIMEOUT=0, but the nested-niri checks ran the shell on Qt's 100 ms default, so a loaded builder's late frame callbacks had Qt take the cat's window for hidden and draw it again as each came. With the timeout set to 5 ms, an idle lender failed this case the same way, 17 frames, and two other frame-count cases with it. The fix has every check built by shellOnNiri read the setting from the unit, and has the cat follow every frame of a walk rather than ask of frames one by one, which drew a frame with each ask; the two landed together, so which of them ended the held walk's frames isn't told apart. The net runs this check at most heads that move the shell, 20 to 55 times a day from 18 to 22 Nov. The closed row's failures, 3 in 66 runs and not yet read, end the same run of twenty, so twenty in a row take about 34 runs, one to two days while main moves. While it stands, nothing catches the cat drawing or stepping under the launcher, or its walk not going on from where it was held. Its owner moves the due and says why before this date if a run fails

Its owner, XY9H5C, who owns the margin cat, takes the second move's case off with the entry above, and by 2026-11-26 23:00 UTC finds why the closed row's way off begins turns, lands or hangs, moving this due and saying why before then if it hasn't. The second move's failures were the case's rule, found on 23 Nov: the cat peeking 3 rows down from the gap at y -5 was next said at 816 and 845, carried by its ground as the slide back took the gap off the screen's foot. The case now counts such a place as where it got to only on a move back up, a ride or a way across to a seat, which sets off from there (a builder's run on 23 Nov began its way across with a fall, laid 2 px off the gap), and only a gap between workspaces below it, off by as far as the cat says niri's slide still had its ground, give or take two of its sizes. That holds only where the ride began, since the cat says how far its ground is off; a way across is held only where it sets off, and each later place on the ride is held to the way it was laid and its ground to never being carried farther off, which assumes the theme's spring never overshoots, and how far its ground is off is proven frame by frame in Qt's engine. The closed row's failures are not yet read; the frame callback timeout the entry above names may bear on them, which is untested. The closed row's case failed on main at 0e420d94fa78 twice and f76d551d20c1, its way off beginning turns, lands rather than rides, lands, shakes, and once hanging 1.16 s, passing between, in 3 of the net's 66 runs of the check from 20 to 22 Nov; the fourth failing run of either case, at 1e68b60f40fe, was the second move's alone. At 3 in 66 twenty pass by luck about two times in five, so the count alone can't show its fix: the fix also names the cause it found, as one of those failing runs' logs shows it, and keeps what the case asserts. While it stands, nothing here catches a closed row's fall hanging, being shoved or not landing on the window left, or a second move putting the cat where it never got to or not moving it on; MarginCatFalls.js's cases in Qt's engine still prove the fall frame by frame
reason: failed on main at 0e420d94fa78, f76d551d20c1 and 1e68b60f40fe, passing between, under builder load
